4559.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *árktos, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂ŕ̥tḱos (“bear”). Cognates include Latin ursus, Welsh arth, Sanskrit ऋक्ष (ṛ́kṣa), Old Armenian արջ (arǰ), and Albanian ari.

4553.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₂élbʰit. Cognates include Albanian elb.

4556.t: From ἀ- (a-, “not”) + πεῖρα (peîra, “trial, attempt”) + -ος (-os). Compare with Latin peritus.

4555.t: From Proto-Hellenic *aksōn, from Proto-Indo-European *h₂eḱs-. Cognate with Mycenaean Greek 𐀀𐀒𐀰𐀚 (a-ko-so-ne), Sanskrit अक्ष (akṣa, “axle, axis, balance beam”) and Latin axis.

4549.t: From ἅλς (háls, “salt, sea”) + -εύς (-eús, suffix for person concerned).

4511.t: From ἀν- (an-, “not”) + ὄφελος (óphelos, “advantage, help”) + -ης (-ēs, adjective suffix).

4558.t: From ἀ- (a-, not) + πίμπλημι (pímplēmi, “to fill full, satisfy, satiate”) + -τος (-tos).

4563.t: Uncertain. Beekes hesitantly suggest a derivation from Proto-Indo-European *g⁽ʷ⁾ow- (“hand”).

4533.t: From ἀπο- (apo-, “away, from, off”) + τρέπω (trépō, “turn”) from Proto-Indo-European *trep-.

4526.t: From ἀπο- (apo-, “to, toward”) + σβέννυμι (sbénnūmi, “to quench, to be quenched”).

4519.t: From ἀπαλλάσσω (apallássō, “to release, deliver”) + -σείω (-seíō, desiderative suffix)
